en: The Legend of the Elder Anulepadāyaka The Chapter on the Parasols, Number Six I offered a fragrant ointment to the Buddha, the Great Sage, the Teacher of the World. By that merit, I have attained the state of an Arhat, free from all defilements. Having abandoned birth and death, I have reached the end of existence. I have attained the coolness of Nibbāna; my task is done. I have paid my debt and am free from all obligations. I have laid down the heavy burden and attained the supreme goal. Through this offering of fragrant ointment, I have now reached the final state. This is the true fruit of giving. Thus it was said. Thus ends the legend of the Elder Anulepadāyaka.
“At the Bodhi tree of the Sage Anomadassī,
I offered a lump of sweet rice.”
I performed manual labor.
Having seen that well-executed work,
Anomadassi, the supreme among men, said:
Standing amidst the community of bhikkhus,
the Teacher spoke this verse:
“By this good deed, [one attains]...”
And through his volition and aspiration,
having experienced prosperity,
he will bring an end to suffering.”
With a serene facial complexion,
one-pointed and well-composed,
I bear this final body.
In the teaching of the Perfectly Enlightened One,
one hundred kalpas ago,
when it was complete and without deficiency, I existed.
The king named Sabbaghana was a wheel-turning monarch of great power.
He possessed the four analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā).
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Anulepadāyaka speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Anulepadāyaka is the sixth.
